note: Declared in src/reporting/architecture.py and verified at export time: every step below names a module that exists and an outputs/ directory that exists.

steps.title: Corpus ingest and audit
steps.summary: Four public corpora are opened, counted and checksummed against what their documentation claims. Where the two disagree, the files win and the discrepancy is recorded rather than reconciled quietly.

steps.title: Label harmonisation and subject grouping
steps.summary: Five label spaces are kept separate, never merged, and every recording is attached to a subject where one can be derived. The subject, not the recording, is what a fold splits on.
steps.rule: No subject leakage: a subject never appears in both train and test.

steps.title: Mono conversion and resampling to 2 kHz
steps.summary: Recordings arrive at 44.1 kHz, 4 kHz and 2 kHz. All are reduced to mono and resampled to a common 2 kHz, which retains the whole diagnostic band of a heart sound and discards the rest.

steps.title: Signal quality assessment
steps.summary: Clipping, silence and a signal-to-noise proxy are measured here, in the middle of the chain, because the band-pass deletes the out-of-band term the proxy needs and normalisation deletes the levels the other two are defined against.

steps.title: Band-pass filtering
steps.summary: A zero-phase band-pass keeps the murmur band and removes mains hum, handling noise and the low-frequency wander that breathing and handling put into a chest recording.

steps.title: Amplitude normalisation
steps.summary: Recordings differ by stethoscope, gain and chest wall. Normalisation removes the loudness difference so that a feature describes the sound rather than the microphone.

steps.title: Feature extraction, 138 across six families
steps.summary: Time-domain, spectral, MFCC, chroma, wavelet and envelope descriptors are computed per recording. The registry is fixed: the same 138 columns in the same order for every corpus and every experiment.

steps.title: Fold-local imputation and scaling
steps.summary: The imputer and the scaler are fitted on the training fold only and then applied to the held-out fold. Fitting either on the full matrix would leak the test fold's distribution into training.
steps.rule: Fold safety: nothing is fitted on data the outer test fold contributed to.

steps.title: Feature selection inside the training fold
steps.summary: Which of the 138 features survive is itself decided per fold, from the training rows only. A selector chosen once on the whole matrix is one of the commonest ways a published result becomes unreproducible.
steps.rule: Fold safety: the selector never sees the outer test fold.

steps.title: Hyperparameter search, nested
steps.summary: Genetic, swarm, Bayesian and randomised search run in an inner loop over the training fold. The outer fold is never scored during the search, so the reported number is not the number that was optimised.
steps.rule: Fold safety: the search is scored on inner splits only.

steps.title: Weighted soft-voting ensemble
steps.summary: SVM, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting each produce a class probability, and a weighted average of the three produces the vote. The weights are searched per fold under the same fold safety rule.

steps.title: Repeated nested cross-validation and reporting
steps.summary: Every experiment reports sensitivity, specificity, F1, balanced accuracy and AUC across repeated subject-grouped folds. Accuracy alone is never the headline, and model selection prioritises sensitivity and balanced accuracy.
steps.rule: Never accuracy alone: five metrics per binary experiment, always.
